description:
Redwood Inference is updating its enterprise security enablement kit to reduce friction in late-stage sales cycles (security review, procurement) and to standardize answers across Sales, Solutions Engineering, and Security/GRC. The project refreshes three customer-facing deliverables: (1) an updated Security FAQ (aligned to current product reality across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private), (2) a set of compliance and security one-pagers (SOC 2 posture, encryption, SSO/RBAC, audit logging, data residency/retention, subprocessors), and (3) a standardized RFP response library (approved language + evidence pointers + “where to find it” mapping). Scope includes content updates, internal review/approval workflows, and packaging for easy field use (Drive PDFs + Confluence canonical sources). Out of scope: new product/security feature development beyond minor documentation clarifications, and legal contract template rewrites (handled separately by Finance/Legal when needed).

Primary stakeholders: Security & Compliance (Dr. Aisha Rahman, Marcus Lin, Olga Petrov; contributors Kevin Osei, Daniel Carter), Product Security & Compliance PM (Naomi Feldman), Solutions Engineering (Markus Klein and team), and Sales leadership (Jordan Blake; regional VPs Stephanie Nguyen, Lukas Meyer). Secondary stakeholders: Customer Success (for renewals/security reviews), DevEx/docs team for publishing updates to redwood-docs, and RevOps (Isabelle Laurent) for CRM linking.

Planned timeline (6 weeks):
- Week 1: kickoff, inventory of existing FAQ/one-pagers/RFP templates, identify gaps and “source of truth” owners, define review rubric and versioning.
- Weeks 2–3: draft updates in Drive; iterate on controversial items (data retention/residency defaults, audit log scope, Private deployment boundary, incident notification wording).
- Week 4: formal review cycle (Security Engineering + GRC + Product + Solutions Eng), redline and approval, map evidence links (SOC 2 report access process, pen test summaries, security contact).
- Week 5: publish canonical Confluence pages; generate field-ready PDFs; update docs-site snippets where external references are needed.
- Week 6: rollout enablement (Sales training notes, Slack announcements), HubSpot linking, and a maintenance plan (quarterly review + triggers for updates on new controls/features).

Constraints and quality bar: content must be consistent across surfaces (Confluence, Drive PDFs, RFP library, email attachments), clearly separate Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private responsibilities, avoid over-committing (e.g., “always”/“never”), and be reviewable/auditable (version history, owner, last-reviewed date). Some materials are restricted (customer-sensitive evidence process, security exceptions, or shared SOC 2 artifacts) and should be marked accordingly.

Define canonical sources + versioning plan: where the “source of truth” lives (Confluence) vs field packaging (Drive PDFs), and how updates are requested and approved quarterly.
Scope and gap analysis: inventory current security FAQ + RFP answers; list missing topics (data residency, retention controls, audit logging export, SSO/SAML details, subprocessors).
Docs-site updates needed to support enablement kit: refresh security/compliance public docs snippets and link targets referenced in FAQ/RFP responses (no product changes).
Create/refresh internal evidence pointer index (internal-only): where to find SOC 2 letter, pen test summary, subprocessor list, and audit log schemas for reviewers.
Lightweight formatting template for one-pagers (consistent structure, tables, callouts, footer version stamp) to be applied to Drive PDFs and Confluence pages.

Published Security FAQ v2: product-specific answers (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), encryption, key management options, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, vulnerability management, incident comms, and support SLAs; includes approved wording and “last reviewed” info.
Changelog for the Security FAQ: version history, summary of edits, and links to review approvals (Security Engineering + GRC + Product).
Internal positioning guide for AEs/SEs: how to frame Redwood’s security posture, deployment modes, shared responsibility boundaries, and common objections during security review.
Appendix content guidance to be used in security-focused decks: standardized slides for encryption, audit logging, SSO/RBAC, data residency, and compliance program overview.
Internal SOP: how to handle security questionnaires and evidence requests (SOC 2 access flow, NDA requirements, who can share what, turnaround SLAs, escalation path). Marked restricted.
Customer-facing one-pager: region availability, residency controls by deployment mode, logs/telemetry handling, and how Dedicated/Private change data flow.
Customer-facing one-pager: retention defaults, configurable retention where available, deletion requests process, and audit log retention considerations.
Customer-facing one-pager: what is logged, log schema categories, export options (SIEM), and differences across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
Customer-facing one-pager: SSO/SAML support, SCIM (if applicable), role models, admin controls, and recommended enterprise setup patterns.
Detailed RBAC reference for security reviews: roles/permissions matrix, least-privilege guidance, and auditability notes.
Customer-facing summary of Secure SDLC: code review, CI controls, dependency scanning, vulnerability remediation SLAs, and release processes.
Customer-facing one-pager: incident detection/triage, customer notification approach, and where status updates are published; avoids over-commitments and clarifies contract-dependent timelines.
Internal process doc: how Sales/SEs request security appendix updates, who approves language, and how redlines are tracked and stored.
Canonical RFP response library: approved boilerplate answers, evidence pointers, “Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private” variants, and guidance on when to route to Security/GRC or Legal.
Working outline for the kit refresh: section map, required one-pagers, owners, open questions, and notes on what’s outdated.
Draft Security FAQ v2 with tracked edits notes, unresolved questions, and placeholders for evidence links before Confluence publication.
Slide-based one-pager pack draft: each slide is a one-pager (SOC 2, encryption, SSO/RBAC, audit logs, retention/residency) with reviewer comments.
Spreadsheet question bank: common security questionnaire prompts, mapped to approved answers, owner, evidence link, and last-reviewed date.
GRC working doc: detailed instructions for sharing SOC 2 materials under NDA, including email templates and approval checklist. Likely restricted.
Compilation of AE/SE feedback: confusing questions encountered, customer pushback themes, and requested clarifications to incorporate into FAQ/RFP responses.
Final exported PDF of the Security FAQ v2 for field sharing; version-stamped and aligned to Confluence canonical content.
Final exported PDF pack of compliance/security one-pagers for sending to prospects during security review.
